title: Democratic participation in the EU is constrained by unfamiliarity with participatory tools and an information environment where distrust and AI opacity are central concerns
source_unit: European Commission, Special Eurobarometer 568: Protecting and Promoting Democracy, fielded November 2025 and catalogued in 2026
geography: European Union citizens across the 27 Member States

denominator.unit: Special Eurobarometer 568 EU27 public-opinion survey frame

participatory_unfamiliarity.unit: percent saying they are not very or not at all familiar with activities such as citizens' assemblies or participatory planning

information_transparency_incentive.unit: percent identifying more transparency and access to information about ways to participate as the strongest encouragement to direct involvement in EU policymaking

local_debates_incentive.unit: percent identifying more local-level debates as an encouragement to participation

direct_participation_incentive.unit: percent identifying more opportunities for direct participation as an encouragement

participation_route.value: institutional participation may be limited not only by willingness but by low familiarity and weak visibility of how participation works

observations.method: European Commission Special Eurobarometer 568 public-opinion survey across the EU27, with country and EU aggregate data available through the European Data Portal.
observations.uncertainty: Familiarity is not the same as access, desire, or ability to participate; the survey does not measure whether particular citizens' assemblies produced policy influence.
observations.subgroup: EU citizens, civil-society organizations, local authorities, participatory-democracy practitioners, policymakers, and people unfamiliar with formal participation channels.
observations.counterinterpretation: Low familiarity may reflect limited exposure rather than institutional failure; local debates or informal civic activity can provide participation outside named EU mechanisms.

observations.period: November 2025; perceived challenges to EU democracy

denominator.unit: Special Eurobarometer 568 EU27 public-opinion survey frame

institutional_distrust.unit: percent identifying growing public distrust toward democratic institutions and processes as a serious challenge

foreign_information_manipulation.unit: percent identifying foreign information manipulation, interference, and disinformation, including around elections, as a serious challenge

ai_political_opacity.unit: percent identifying lack of transparency about whether political content online is promoted through technologies such as AI as a serious challenge

challenge_route.value: institutional distrust, foreign information operations, and opaque AI-mediated political visibility are experienced as linked democratic risks

observations.method: EU27 public-opinion survey questions on democratic threats, information manipulation, and AI-related political transparency.
observations.uncertainty: Perceived seriousness does not identify exposure, source, or causal influence; respondents may interpret distrust, disinformation, and AI opacity differently across countries and languages.
observations.subgroup: EU citizens, voters, political parties, media organizations, platforms, election authorities, regulators, and civil-society fact-checkers.
observations.counterinterpretation: Concern can reflect increased awareness rather than deteriorating conditions; transparency rules may improve confidence without eliminating manipulation or partisan distrust.

observations.period: November 2025; informed elections and information quality

denominator.unit: Special Eurobarometer 568 EU27 public-opinion survey frame

accurate_accessible_information.unit: percent identifying accurate and accessible information for informed choices as the most important element of free and fair elections

equitable_media_coverage.unit: percent identifying equitable media coverage for candidates and parties and campaigns not marked by disinformation as most important

election_disinformation_concern.unit: percent concerned about voters basing decisions on disinformation

cyberattack_concern.unit: percent concerned about cyberattacks influencing elections

foreign_influence_concern.unit: percent concerned about foreign countries influencing elections

election_route.value: citizens place information accessibility and accuracy alongside media fairness and election-security defenses

observations.method: EU27 public-opinion survey on free and fair elections, information quality, disinformation, cyberattacks, and foreign influence.
observations.uncertainty: Concern levels are not incident rates or measured election effects; priorities may differ by national media system, electoral experience, and exposure to political content.
observations.subgroup: Voters, journalists, candidates, parties, election authorities, cybersecurity institutions, platforms, and citizens seeking reliable political information.
observations.counterinterpretation: High concern may motivate resilience and media-literacy demand rather than reduce turnout or trust; better information access requires both supply and audience capability.

denominator.unit: Special Eurobarometer 568 EU27 public-opinion survey frame

participation_visibility.value: information about how to participate is identified more often than simply adding participation opportunities as a reason citizens would get involved

local_proximity.value: more local debates to address local matters rank as a stronger participation incentive than more direct EU-level opportunities

institutional_route.value: democratic resilience depends on making participation legible, proximate, and connected to trustworthy information

governance_implication.value: the public-information environment and participatory process design are linked rather than separate democracy interventions

observations.method: Cross-item synthesis of Special Eurobarometer 568 findings on familiarity, participation incentives, distrust, information quality, and election threats.
observations.uncertainty: This is an analytic synthesis of survey items, not a tested causal model of participation or democratic resilience.
observations.subgroup: Citizens, local and EU institutions, civil society, election bodies, educators, media-literacy organizations, and digital platforms.
observations.counterinterpretation: Information transparency can become performative if institutions do not show how participation changes decisions; local proximity may help but cannot replace national or EU-level accountability.

related_sources.claim: The European Commission Eurobarometer survey detail page provides the Special Eurobarometer 568 report and documents.
The Digital Decade 2026 Special Eurobarometer provides complementary public-opinion context on AI, digital sovereignty, online safety, and disinformation.

boundary: This record adds EU public-opinion evidence on familiarity with participatory democracy, distrust, foreign information manipulation, AI transparency, election information quality, cyberattacks, and foreign influence. It is aggregate survey evidence, not respondent-level ingestion, an incident dataset, an election forecast, a platform audit, or proof that transparency alone restores trust.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official European Data Portal record for Special Eurobarometer 568 reviewed for participation familiarity and incentives, democratic challenges, election-information priorities, disinformation, cyberattack, foreign-influence, and AI-transparency measures.
